sections.h2: A video file only fits one wall

items.b: Screens are never the same twice
items.p: Ratio, resolution and loop length differ at every site. A work written in code is re-exported at 32:9, 16:9 or 9:16 from the same source, and pushed up to 4K or 5K. A delivered video file has to be remade each time the screen changes.

items.b: The approved concept is the delivered work
items.p: Our works are deterministic: the same seed on the same canvas always produces the same frames. What you sign off on is what arrives.

items.b: The screen can change every day
items.p: Wire a public API or an institutional database into the work and the wall reads differently each morning without anyone editing anything.

Commissioned video work usually runs a month or more. Ours takes a week to three concepts, because planning, copy, visuals and playback code are generated together from your house colours, typefaces and restrictions.

pages.h1: From the concept to the cable
pages.lead: A media facade fails in the gap between the people who make the content and the people who mount the screen. We do both, so there is no gap to fall into.

aside.t: Written as code, re-rendered per screen

items.p: We measure the surface — ratio, resolution, viewing distance, ambient brightness, and what the wall is made of. For projection we confirm throw distance and the mapping surface.
Your colours, typefaces and any restricted imagery are registered as production constraints first. Three concepts follow within one week.
The approved concept is rendered at the site's exact pixel dimensions. Because the work is code, changing the wall does not mean remaking the work.
Panels, projectors, mounting, cabling, and the playback machine. Handed over running.
Content is swapped for seasons and events. Where a public API is wired in, the screen changes on its own.

sections.caption: Common signage formats and what suits them
rows: Very large, seen from far away and at night. Slow movement, high contrast, no small type.
Bright ambient light. Saturated colour and thick strokes survive daylight; fine detail does not.
Seen close, for a long time, by people waiting. Quiet, dense, non-repetitive.
The eye travels left to right. Horizon-based work reads; centre-weighted work leaves the ends empty.
Read looking up. Vertical flow works; anything that gathers in the centre leaves the top and bottom bare.
Close range, single viewer. Fine detail is worth it here.

sections.p: Pick whichever fits the equipment you already have.

sections.h2: Questions we are asked before signing

items.q: How long until we see something?
items.a: Three concepts within one week of the brief. Commissioned video work usually runs a month or more; ours is shorter because the media art is written in code rather than assembled in an editor. Your colours, typefaces and restrictions are registered as production constraints first, then planning, copy, visuals and playback code are generated together.

items.q: Why does it matter that it is code?
items.a: Because every screen is a different shape. A work written in code is re-exported at 32:9, 16:9 and 9:16 from one source and pushed to 4K or 5K. A delivered video file has to be remade whenever the screen changes. Our works are also deterministic — the same seed on the same canvas always produces the same frames — so the approved concept and the delivered work cannot drift apart.

items.q: Can the screen show live data?
items.a: Yes. Public APIs and institutional databases are wired into the work, so the same piece reads differently each day — air quality, weather, visitor counts, whatever the institution already collects. Ordinary signage players cannot do this; they play a fixed playlist. This runs on a player we set up.

Installation is carried out in person across Daegu, Gyeongbuk, Busan, Gyeongnam and Ulsan. Beyond that we arrange it around the travel schedule. Content-only delivery has no geographic limit — the file arrives by download.

items.q: We already have a panel. Can you just supply content?
items.a: Yes, and that is the most common case. Tell us the panel's pixel dimensions and we render to them exactly. If the panel has no reliable player, we can set one up and connect it over HDMI.

sections.p: A photograph and a rough measurement are enough to start.

pages.title: ArtWork Studio: Make a Media Art Screen Yourself | Oneul-eun Bomnal
pages.description: Pick a generative media art screen, see a five-second watermarked sample at once, and hang it on a photograph of real signage at true scale. No sign-up. From 100,000 won.
pages.h1: You choose the screen. We render it.
pages.lead: No sign-up, no account. Screens we have already built are shown to you; pick one you like. A five-second watermarked sample appears at once, and you can hang it on a photograph of real signage to judge the scale before you buy.

items.p: Thirty-odd subjects — a bamboo grove, a moon jar, an inlaid celadon, a golden Buddha wall, a reaction-diffusion field. Press again and the same subject comes back different. Nothing is a stock loop.
Enter the real pixel dimensions and the loop length. The work is redrawn at that ratio rather than stretched to fit.
Your choice is mapped onto photographs of real signage — a city hall board, a lobby column, a two-sided column, a building frontage — at true scale, so you can see how large it actually reads.
The final render arrives within 24 business hours on business days. Every work carries a number; the same number always redraws the same screen.

₩3.9M for four seasonal works · ₩9M for ten works a year, with your colours, logo and typeface registered as a template.
₩1.5M. Ships with the work loaded. Plug in HDMI and it plays on power-up, with no internet connection.

sections.html: A note on language. ArtWork Studio's own interface is currently in Korean. The controls are largely visual — you press a tile, you get a screen — and every work carries a number you can quote back to us in English. If you would rather not use the tool at all, describe what you want on the contact page and we will send concepts instead.

Everything is drawn by our code. No photographs or video are composited in. Works that show three-dimensional form take vertex coordinates from public-domain (CC0) models and redraw them as lines and points in our own code — no one else's image is ever output. Samples shown in the tool are not stored and may not be used commercially.

sections.p: It costs nothing to look. The interface is Korean; the screens are not.

sections.h2: The events it is built for

items.p: Events that only run after dark. Media art and darkness keep the same hours.
A moving background appears where people are already standing to take photographs.
There is no reason to mount and strip a permanent screen for a single day.
Used to test a wall before committing to a permanent installation.

items.a: ₩5,000,000 for a base rental of three days. That includes media art made for your institution and both installation and strike, so there is no separate content commission. We install the day before the event. Each further day is ₩1,000,000 — the content already exists by then, so only the projector and equipment are charged. That is why the per-day cost falls on multi-day festivals.

items.q: Why is three days the minimum?
items.a: Because we install the day before. Arriving on the morning of the event leaves no time to set focus and brightness against the actual ambient light. Hanging it the day before and switching it on once after dark is what makes it look right on the day. Even a single-day event is booked as three, covering the install day and the strike.

items.q: We have no footage to play. Can we still book?
items.a: Yes, and the content is included in the base price. Tell us about the institution and we make the media art for it. If you already hold footage, we re-render it to the screen's dimensions instead. Because we build in code rather than editing video, the same work comes back out at whatever ratio and resolution the site needs.

items.q: Does someone have to be on site?
items.a: No. The player starts on power-up and keeps running. If playback stops it notices and restarts itself. No keyboard and no trained operator are needed at the venue.

items.q: Will it work outdoors with no wall?
items.a: That is what it is for. It projects onto tents, booths and bare walls. Being short-throw, it produces a 3m image in spaces with no room to stand back. It can hang from a frame or sit on the ground.
Daegu and Gyeongbuk first, then Busan, Gyeongnam and Ulsan — we install and strike in person. Beyond that we arrange it around the travel schedule.
